provenance.note: `Credentials` takes a whole `SignifyClient`, so the real client is driven with `globalThis.fetch` replaced by a recorder that signs its answers as a KERIA agent would. The identifier and credential every lookup answers with are the pinned unit test's own `mockGetAID` and `mockCredential`, read from `test/app/test-utils.ts` by the reference's own compiler. The clock is pinned because `issue` and `revoke` both default their timestamp to a clock reading; key material derives at the reference's production Argon2 profile, and each sealed salt is masked as `<SXLT>` and recorded by what it opens to. `PUBLIC TEST MATERIAL`: the passcode is the pinned tests' own and has never protected anything.

declarations.list_body: data = { filter: filtr, sort: sort, skip: skip, limit: limit, }
declarations.get_headers: headers = includeCESR ? new Headers({ Accept: 'application/json+cesr' }) : new Headers({ Accept: 'application/json' })
declarations.get_return: return includeCESR ? await res.text() : await res.json();
declarations.issue_est_only_throw: throw new Error('Establishment only not implemented');
declarations.issue_subject: [, subject] = Saider.saidify({ d: '', ...args.a, dt: args.a.dt ?? new Date().toISOString().replace('Z', '000+00:00'), })
declarations.issue_acdc: [, acdc] = Saider.saidify({ v: versify(Protocols.ACDC, undefined, Serials.JSON, 0), d: '', u: args.u, i: args.i ?? hab.prefix, ri: args.ri, s: args.s, a: subject, e: args.e, r: args.r, })
declarations.issue_iss: [, iss] = Saider.saidify({ v: versify(Protocols.KERI, undefined, Serials.JSON, 0), t: Ilks.iss, d: '', i: acdc.d, s: '0', ri: args.ri, dt: subject.dt, })
declarations.issue_anchor: anc = interact({ pre: hab.prefix, sn: sn + 1, data: [ { i: iss.i, s: iss.s, d: iss.d, }, ], dig: hab.state.d, version: undefined, kind: undefined, })
declarations.issue_body: body = { acdc: acdc, iss: iss, ixn: anc.sad, sigs, [keeper.algo]: keeper.params(), }
declarations.revoke_registry_lookup: if ('ri' in cred.sad && cred.sad.ri !== undefined) { registryId = cred.sad.ri; } else if ('rd' in cred.sad && cred.sad.rd !== undefined) { registryId = cred.sad.rd; } else { throw new Error('Neither ri nor rd property found in credential'); }
declarations.revoke_rev: _rev = { v: vs, t: Ilks.rev, d: '', i: said, s: '1', ri: registryId, p: cred.status.d, dt: dt, }
declarations.revoke_body: body = { rev: rev, ixn: ixn, sigs: sigs, [keeper.algo]: keeper.params(), }
declarations.credential_schema: Credential: { sad: | components['schemas']['ACDC_V_1'] | components['schemas']['ACDC_V_2']; atc: string; iss: components['schemas']['IssEvent']; issatc: string; pre: string; schema: components['schemas']['Schema']; chains: { [key: string]: unknown; }[]; status: components['schemas']['CredentialState']; anchor: components['schemas']['Anchor']; anc: components['schemas']['KeyEvent']; ancatc: string[]; };

notes.list: `list` is the only read in the family that is a `POST`: its filter, sort, skip, and limit become a JSON body sent to `/credentials/query`, and all four are written whether or not the caller supplied them
notes.get: `get` takes a boolean second parameter with four overload signatures, and selects between `res.json()` and `res.text()` on it — the same call returns two unrelated types
notes.delete: `delete` calls `fetch` with three arguments, so its `data` is `undefined` and `JSON.stringify(undefined)` leaves the request with no body at all
notes.issue: `issue` addresses `hab.name` — the alias the **agent** answered with — rather than the `name` the caller asked for, and defaults the credential's issuer to `hab.prefix` without ever checking a supplied one
notes.revoke: `revoke` reads the credential back from the agent to learn its registry and its prior digest, so it cannot build a revocation offline, and writes the sequence number as the literal `'1'`

shortfall.note: the reference's own mocks do not satisfy the schema its production code casts to. `mockGetAID` carries no `icp_dt`, which `HabState` declares required, so this generator adds one — nothing derived reads it, so no recorded byte changes. `mockCredential` is missing seven of the eleven fields `Credential` declares and carries two the schema does not, and `Credentials.get` hands it to a caller as a credential anyway; that one is recorded rather than repaired, and the Rust side is shown refusing it.

mock_records.note: the records every lookup answers with. The identifier is the reference's own `mockGetAID` with `icp_dt` added; its sealed salt is masked as `<SXLT>` and recorded by what it opens to, because a fresh ephemeral key seals it every run, so the Rust side seals that salt again with the same controller key before reloading a keeper from the record.

pinned_confirmations.note: the pinned `credentialing.test.ts` exercises all six methods in one case, asserting each path, each method, and — for `issue` and `revoke` — the fields of each body. Its identifier is `mockGetAID` and its credential is `mockCredential`, both read here from `test/app/test-utils.ts` by the reference's own compiler, so every value in this fixture is one the reference's own suite asserts against. What it does **not** assert is any exact body: `issue` and `revoke` both read the clock, so the test checks fields rather than bytes. Pinning the clock is what makes the bytes reproducible here.
